findings.title: canManage() grants manage to admins with only view permission
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (no-arg) returns hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so an admin granted only the 'view' scope on all Groups passes requireManage(). GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() relies on requireManage() to create top-level groups, so a view-only FGAP admin can create groups (and any other caller of groups().requireManage()/canManage()). It should check MANAGE only, like canManage(GroupModel) does.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs, not group IDs
findings.body: In V2 a specific group resource's name is the group id (see hasPermission(), which looks it up with resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)), while Resource.getId() is the internal authorization-store id. getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() passes groupResource.getId() into hasPermission(), so the findByName lookup misses the specific resource and falls back to the all-groups resource, and it adds groupResource.getId() to the returned set. Callers such as UsersResource.searchForUser() and BruteForceUsersResource put that set into UserModel.GROUPS to restrict the user query to those group ids, so the query is restricted by non-group ids (returning no members) or not restricted per-group at all. It should use groupResource.getName() both for the lookup and for the returned group id.

findings.title: hasPermission can NPE when the all-groups resource does not exist
findings.body: When no specific group resource is found, hasPermission() calls AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource(), which returns null if the 'Groups' resource-type resource has not been created (e.g. admin permissions not initialized for the realm), and then immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and later resource.getScopes() with that null resource. This turns a simple permission check (canView/canManage/canViewMembers, invoked on ordinary group/user listing paths) into a NullPointerException/500 instead of returning false. A null check after getResourceTypeResource() is needed.
